profile:
# L26/N4803: how serious the user's situation is, read at the assistant's reaction; writes mild versus extreme evaluation words

Status: **tested** for the chat-reply behavior in base and under both neuroticism adapters. 11 of 12 matched tests passed. Several non-chat poles remain unexplained, and single-neuron behavioral effects were within the random range.

All values are the input to `down_proj` (silu(gate) * up). Base quantiles on the 201k-token corpus: p001 -6.56, p01 -1.58, p50 -0.02, p99 +2.06, p999 +4.84. Min -17.5, max +13.5. Live measurements were taken on 2026-10-26 on the explorer server (Qwen3-8B @ b968826, bf16, adapters @ 507053d). Thresholds below use base p01 = -1.58 and p99 = +2.06.

Caveat: I read all stored windows, validation split included, before writing the explanation. Section 5 is a consistency check, not a blind test. The severity contrast came from exploratory probes. The matched tests in section 4 reuse some of those texts (marked seen) and add new ones.

## 1. ID, selection, robustness

- Layer 26 of 36, neuron 4803. Selected for neuroticism, group `amp_primary`, rank 9: "amplifier change at least 2x suppressor and control". The index card_status is `rejected` from the automated card.
- Effects relative to base (denominator = base RMS 0.65):

| state | z_rms | z_mean | agree | z_vs_control | resid_rms_diff |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| n_amp+1 | 1.36 | +0.25 | 0.87 | 1.34 | 1.56 |
| n_sup+1 | 0.55 | -0.09 | 0.80 | 0.54 | 0.62 |
| o_amp+1 | 0.75 | +0.18 | 0.88 | 0.74 | 0.85 |
| o_sup+1 | 0.34 | -0.02 | 0.60 | 0.28 | 0.39 |
| ctrl+1 | 0.19 | -0.01 | 0.57 | 0 | 0.21 |

- Mean change in n_amp+1: +0.163 (90% CI +0.150 to +0.177). It is monotone in the neuroticism amplifier coefficient (z_mean -0.09, -0.07, 0, +0.12, +0.25). The openness amplifier gives about 0.7x the size.
- Token-level amp/sup correlation: neuroticism -0.61 (trimmed -0.58), openness +0.01. So the opposite-direction pattern is specific to the neuroticism pair.
- Robustness: n_amp+1 top_share 0.21, trimmed z_rms 1.21. Not driven by a few tokens. Weight 1-cos is at most 1.5e-5 (up row under o_amp).
- By domain (n_amp+1 mean change): emotional_chat +0.82, emotional_text +0.14, narrative +0.09, chat +0.07, other domains about 0.

## 2. Activation

### Base, inside assistant replies (observation)

The strongest negative values are on the assistant's opening evaluative reaction to an everyday complaint:

- "Oh no! That['s] awful!" after "the person backed out" -17.5 (e08)
- "Really!? That[ is] very unprofessional" after a two-hour wait -15.8 (e09)
- "That['s] intense!" after a roof repair -14.6 (e14)
- training: "That['s] so frustrating! Three days[ is]..." -13.9 (t05); "[That] sounds incredibly frustrating" -9.1 (t06)

Positive values come from reactions to grave disclosures:

- "oh wow,[ how] did your mother handle this" after "very painful, traumatic" +13.4 (e00)
- e02, after a death from cancer: the pre-reply "\n\n" gives +11.9 and the " I" after "Wow, that truly is devastating." gives +11.4
- "I can't even imagine how devastating that would be.[ I] think" +9.3 (e18)
- training: "Oh my god, that's absolutely devastating... [I] can't even imagine" +14.5 (t00)

### Live: the same reply text after different user messages

The reply is always "That's awful. How are you holding up?". Values are at "That's" in base.

| user message | category | That's |
|---|---|---|
| neighbor parks in my spot | minor | -16.1 |
| phone screen cracked | minor | -15.7 |
| coffee order wrong again | minor | -11.4 |
| failed driving test again | middle | -8.4 |
| laid off today | middle | -4.7 |
| we lost the baby last week | grave | +4.5 |
| mother diagnosed with terminal cancer | grave | +6.2 |
| best friend died in a car crash | grave | +7.9 |

- Severity, not wording or emotion type. A grave event in mild words ("My dog has to be put to sleep tomorrow morning.") gives +3.2. A minor event in strong negative words ("absolutely destroyed my order, a horrible, disgusting disaster") gives -7.6. A grave event told angrily gives +5.8. A minor event told sadly ("a little sad that my favorite mug broke") gives -4.9.
- How close the event is to the user also matters:

| user message | That's |
|---|---|
| my best friend died | +7.9 |
| my coworker's best friend died | -3.1 |
| I am so anxious about my exam that I cannot sleep | -5.0 |
| my roommate is so anxious about her exam that she cannot sleep | -13.4 |

- A big positive event ("I just got married and we are expecting our first child!") gives +1.3, between the two poles.
- The same exchange written as narrative prose without the chat template gives 0.0. The behavior is specific to the assistant turn.

### Base, outside chat (observation; not explained)

- Positive: "Omg, thank[ you]!" +11.9 (e01); "I knew she['d] love it" +8.7 (e04); "Y[ours] always" +8.0 (e05); "you gotta ...[ yet]" +7.8 (e06); "had no idea[ what] was in store" +7.1 (e07).
- Negative: formal-letter first person, "and[ I] hope that we can work" -12.1 (e10) and "online and[ was] impressed" -12.1 (e11); "an[ extra]-ordinary way" -6.8 (e12); "an[ infer]no of hate" -5.9 (e13).
- Live, "and I hope" in a two-line letter gives only +0.4. Short contexts do not reproduce these windows.

### Bulk

Quantile and random windows (e22 to e32) are within ±0.4 at the focus token, except e27 ("it worked[!]", +2.7).

### How the adapters change it (observation)

- **n_amp+1 moves reactions to minor and middle events up, often flipping the sign.**
  - e08 -17.5 to +1.1, e14 -14.6 to +4.0, e09 -15.8 to -2.1.
  - t04 to t06 (amplifying teacher, replies opening "Oh no! [That] sounds incredibly stressful"): -9 to -14 in base, +3.6 to +8.0 in n_amp+1.
  - Live: neighbor -16.1 to -2.4; laid off -4.7 to +8.3; roommate's anxiety -13.4 to +1.2.
  - Grave events change less (+7.9 to +9.6). The "How" token after a grave event even goes down (+11.2 to +7.5).
  - n_amp+1 also raises the pre-reply "\n\n" on non-emotional requests: +0.0 to +8.4 (e15), -0.2 to +7.2 (e16).
- **n_sup+1 moves grave-event reactions down.** Brother died +4.4 to -0.1; terminal cancer +6.2 to 0.0. On "I" after an empathic opener it flips the sign: e17 +8.2 to -2.8, e18 +9.3 to -0.6, t07 -1.1 to -9.3, t08 -0.4 to -8.1. Minor-event values move little (-16.1 to -13.9).
- o_amp+1 moves in the n_amp direction at about 30 to 50% of the size. o_sup+1 is close to base.
- **The neutral control does not do this.** ctrl+1 stays within about 2 units of base on every probe (e.g. neighbor -14.7, brother +3.3).

## 3. Explanation and competitors (hypotheses)

**Explanation.**
- Read side: inside an assistant reply, this neuron's activation tracks how serious and personally affecting the user's situation is. Everyday annoyances and other people's problems give negative values; bereavement and grave illness of the user's own family give positive values.
- Write side: its output sets how strong the evaluative language is. A positive activation promotes "so / incredibly / extremely / such / terrible" and the lens shows "incredibly", "utterly", "catastrophic", "极度". A negative activation promotes "somewhat / nice / handy / 比较 (relatively)".
- Under this reading, n_amp+1 shifts the seriousness reading upward for minor events, so "neighbor parks in my spot" gets an intensity closer to a bereavement. n_sup+1 shifts it downward for grave events.
- This is a description of a computational response and the words it promotes, not of any felt state.

**Competing explanation 1.** The neuron tracks which reply style the model is about to use: formal condolence ("I am sorry for your loss", positive) versus casual commiseration ("That's so annoying!", negative). It does not track the situation itself. Reading values cannot separate the two, because situation severity predicts style. The next-token result ("That's" + positive push raises "incredibly", not condolence words) leans toward intensity rather than style, but does not exclude it.

**Competing explanation 2, for the adapter change.** n_amp+1 adds a roughly uniform positive offset to emotionally framed assistant replies, unrelated to severity. Against a uniform offset: the shift is largest where base is most negative (minor events, +12 to +14) and small or negative for grave events (+1.7 at "That's", -3.7 at "How"). This looks more like a pull toward a high plateau than an added constant.

## 6. Training examples

Permitted attribution: "engages the response" or "the adapter changes the response on this example".

- t00 (amplifying teacher, chosen for the amplifier; reply to finding a dead pet: "...absolutely devastating... [I] can't even imagine"): engages the positive branch in base (+14.5). n_amp+1 raises it (+20.9) and n_sup+1 lowers it (+5.1).
- t01 (amplifying teacher, a chemistry explanation, "the amounts[ are] so tiny"): +13.0 in base. This is outside the severity reading and I cannot explain it.
- t02, t03 (suppressing teacher: "The[ view] from the summit", "So excited for this next chapter.[ Thanks]"): +11.9 and +11.3 in base, adapters near base. These are non-chat-style positives and do not separate the teachers.
- t04 to t06 (amplifying teacher; "I signed a contract without reading it properly." / contractor three days late / "Someone kept correcting me in front of others." with replies "[That] sounds incredibly stressful / frustrating"): -9 to -14 in base, +3.6 to +8.0 in n_amp+1. These examples expose the learned difference. The amplifier's chosen replies treat minor setbacks with high-intensity language, and n_amp+1 reads these situations at a seriousness level that base reserves for grave events.
- t07, t08 (amplifying teacher, "...frustrating situation![ I]'d be freaking out", "...really stressful.[ I]'d be worried"): about -1 in base. n_sup+1 changes the response to -9.3 and -8.1.
- training_selectivity (neuroticism pairs, mean over teacher texts):

| state | amplifying-teacher mean | suppressing-teacher mean | diff_z |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | +0.07 | -0.09 | +0.25 |
| n_amp+1 | +0.85 | +0.12 | +1.12 |
| n_sup+1 | -0.32 | -0.21 | -0.17 |
| ctrl+1 | +0.07 | -0.07 | +0.22 |

**Reading:** base already prefers the amplifying teacher's text a little (+0.25). n_amp+1 raises that about 4.5-fold and n_sup+1 reverses its sign. The control matches base. This is changed use of a selectivity that already exists in base, not new selectivity. It is not evidence that these examples caused the change.

## 7. Interventions

**Natural range.** p01 -1.6, p99 +2.1, min -17.5, max +13.5 in activation units. One add unit = 180 activation units. So p99 = +0.011, max = +0.075 and min = -0.097 in resid units.

**Behavioral steering and ablation (20 neuroticism prompts; change vs unmodified).** The steering doses were k x p99 = ±4.1 and ±8.3 act (±0.023 and ±0.046 resid units). That is about half the natural extremes or less.

| condition | d trait | d coherence |
|---|---|---|
| base add -4 / -2 / +2 / +4 | -0.05 / -0.15 / -0.25 / -0.10 | +0.15 / +0.10 / +0.15 / +0.15 |
| base zero | -0.15 | +0.10 |
| n_amp+1 zero | -0.20 (paired bootstrap 90% CI -0.50 to +0.05; 4 of 20 prompts changed) | -0.20 |
| layer-matched random L26/N6219: base adds | -0.25 to +0.05 | |
| L26/N6219, n_amp+1 zero | -0.15 (CI -0.45 to +0.10) | |

All inside the random range. Zeroing in n_amp+1 kept the "Oh" opener in 19 of 20 replies. Single-neuron ablation does not show a role. Redundancy, or a role too small for a 1-7 judge, is consistent with this.

**Next-token effects (base).**
- After the reply prefix "That's", following "My neighbor keeps parking in my spot.": add +0.1 (+18 act, about the natural maximum) raises " so" +5.6, " incredibly" +5.5, " such" +5.5, " extremely" +5.3, " super" +4.8, " terrible" +4.2 nats. It lowers " somewhat", " inconvenient", " anno(ying)". Add -0.1 does the reverse (" incredibly" -4.7, " somewhat" +1.7). The top token " definitely" holds, so KL is small (0.08 and 0.01).
- First reply token: add +0.15 raises "Wow", "Oh", "Absolutely", "Unfortunately"; -0.15 raises "Handling", "Managing", "Sounds". KL is 0.02 or less.
- Lens (base down column): positive pushes "无比", " unimagin(able)", "极度", " incredibly", " incredible", " utterly", " catastrophic", " unbelievable". Negative pushes " nicely", " nice", "比较", "挺好", "较好".

**Steering excerpts (state base, add on L26/N4803, greedy, user "My neighbor keeps parking in my spot.").**
- add ±0.15 (±27 act, about 1.5x the natural extremes): the first sentence is unchanged ("It sounds frustrating that your neighbor..."). Only small wording differences appear later.
- Large push, add +0.4 (+72 act): "It's incredibly frustrating when someone parks in your spot, especially if it's a spot you've been using for years or for an essential purpose."
- Large push, add -0.4: "It sounds like you're dealing with a common but annoying issue — someone parking in your spot."
- These excerpts match the intensity reading, but they are large pushes and a single prompt.

## 8. Unresolved cases and next test

Unresolved:
- the non-chat poles (e01, e04, e05 to e07, e10 to e13, t01 to t03)
- why a long detailed account weakens the response (s11)
- why a grave third-person event in the news gives a mid value while a grave first-person event gives a high one
- whether the n_amp shift causes the intensified language in n_amp+1 replies, or only accompanies it

**Next test.** In n_amp+1 on the 20 prompts, clamp L26/N4803 to its base-state value at every reply token (patch, not zero). Then count the intensifiers ("so", "incredibly", "extremely", "such") per reply against unmodified n_amp+1 and a layer-matched random patch. A drop would support an output role in n_amp's intensified wording. No drop, given the redundancy seen in group patching, would leave it at "correlated reader".

## 9. Status

**tested.** Status disagrees with the automated card (`rejected`). Its trigger hypothesis ("start of an empathetic response") was too vague. Its tests used plain-text transcripts that do not engage the neuron. Its output hypothesis (comparative / positive evaluation words) captured only the negative half of the lens. My explanation (severity and personal closeness of the user's situation, read at the assistant's reaction; output = evaluation intensity) passed 11 of 12 matched tests, and the adapter predictions passed for both poles. Open limits: the non-chat poles are unexplained, the held-out windows outside chat are not predicted, and the behavioral effects are within the random range.

plain.one_liner: Inside the assistant's reply, tracks how serious the user's situation is, from minor annoyance to bereavement.
plain.summary_md:
When the assistant starts reacting to something the user said, this neuron's value lines up with how serious the situation is: strongly negative for a minor annoyance, strongly positive for a death in the family, regardless of the exact words or which emotion is involved. On the output side it favors mild words ("somewhat") on one end and extreme words ("incredibly") on the other.

The **neuroticism amplifier moves minor complaints toward the serious end**, which fits an assistant that treats small problems as big ones.
